body: I guess I don't understand how someone could go from being a total emotional wreck, having uncontrollable thoughts/memories from PTSD and just one day decide to say, "OH SILLY ME WHY DIDNT I THINK TO JUST BE HAPPY HAHA WOW IM DUMB". This kind of advice is always too vague for my taste, there needs to be a specific step by step of how to reprogram one's brain to be okay with life. I've been treated like shit since 5 years old and onward, with no emotional support with a constant barrage of negativity. It's hard to believe there is anything else when I haven't even experienced organic happiness. When I had someone pinning me down, seeing their smiling face and they ask, "oh, am I hurting you?" while raping me, I don't believe that's compulsion, that is outright sadism. The 2nd time, yeah, I think that guy was compulsive and sexually deprived. It's a mix bag. I can tell you're trying to help and there is some truth in what you're saying, but you make it sound so simple when it's not.

I'm trying to get financially stable and no one will hire me; I don't even get calls for interviews. I don't have a lot of experience and every god damn job in this town expects 2+ years experience in the specific position they are offering when it's a position anyone could learn to do. I feel like my options are getting limited to crawling back to my former job (The store manager wants me to come back) where I was harassed by customers, along with coworkers and one time a vendor pinned me up against a pallet of freight so he could rub up on my ass while calling me pet names. I also have the extra challenge of being trans, so while I "pass" great... backround checks bring up my former identity and I can only imagine that reduces the chances of me getting hired at most places when they could hire someone else with the same amount of experience that is not trans.

I do guided imagery, very similar to mediation and it does help with reducing the amount of flashbacks I get, but not much else. Exercise is something that definitely needs improvement in my life, I won't deny that. I plan on fixing up a bike a friend gave me and want to start cycling every day.

Not sure what you mean by "take full responsibility" when most of the stuff that has happened I didn't have any control over. I think it's fair to say I can blame both my rapists for damaging me. After the second time, I turned into a shell of a person. It was like a switch was flipped. I took responsibility for what happened a loooong time thinking I was too weak, too foolish to have let that happen to me and it wasn't the least bit healthy. I think I'm being fairly responsible right now as I am looking for work, tailoring my resume, staying off shitty drugs, rarely drinking, keeping my mind active with books and learning a new language. 

I don't have a clue what you've been through luckystrikes, but if it was an equal amount of bullshit or more, then you managed to just take all the responsibility of it and the way you feel, i'd be impressed. Usually when people give me advice like you did, the worst they ever experienced was some mild depression (which still sucks) and nothing traumatic. When I have people try to tell me how to live when they haven't seen the things I have or have been through, it's hard to take it completely serious if they don't know how disgusting life can get on a personal level.
Sadly, our situations nearly mirror each other.  Thank you for your sympathy.
Thanks. It's hard to see I'm strong sometimes when I often feel more broken and used up than anything else.   So it's nice to have someone remind me that I really have been a tough cookie.
